question: How many days of annual leave am I entitled to each year, and how early must I submit the request?

context.title: Annual leave
context.text: An employee is entitled to 28 working days of annual leave in each leave year. Leave requests must be submitted to the Head of Department at least 14 days before the first day of leave.

context.title: Sick leave
context.text: An absence due to illness of more than 3 consecutive days must be supported by a certificate from a registered medical practitioner, submitted when the employee returns to work.

reference: You are entitled to 28 working days of annual leave each leave year, and you must submit the request to your Head of Department at least 14 days before the first day of leave [1].
rubric: Gives 28 working days and the 14-day notice period; cites the annual leave section.

question: How long is maternity leave, and when must I notify my Head of Department?

context.title: Paternity leave
context.text: A male employee is entitled to 5 working days of paternity leave, which must be taken within 7 days of the child's birth.

context.title: Maternity leave
context.text: A female employee is entitled to 84 days of fully paid maternity leave. She notifies the Head of Department in writing at least three months before the expected date of delivery.

reference: Maternity leave is 84 days on full pay. You must notify your Head of Department in writing at least three months before the expected date of delivery [2].
rubric: Gives 84 days on full pay and written notice three months before delivery; cites maternity leave, not paternity.

question: I had a needle-stick injury on the ward. Who do I report it to, and how soon must PEP start?

context.title: Needle-stick and sharps injuries
context.text: Report the injury to the ward in-charge immediately, and in any case within 1 hour. Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) must be started as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after exposure.

context.title: Mandatory training
context.text: Every clinical employee completes an infection prevention and control (IPC) refresher course every 12 months. Completion is recorded in the training register by the IPC focal person.

reference: Report the injury to the ward in-charge immediately, and in any case within 1 hour. PEP must start as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after the exposure [1].
rubric: Report to the ward in-charge within 1 hour; PEP no later than 72 hours; cites the sharps section.

question: Which form do I use to claim the night duty allowance, and what is the deadline?

context.title: Official travel
context.text: Travel outside the duty station must be approved in writing by the Head of Department at least 7 days before departure. The approved travel form is attached to the claim on return.

context.title: Night duty allowance
context.text: Claims are made on form MOH-F12 and must reach the accounts office by the 5th day of the following month. Late claims are paid in the next payroll cycle.

reference: Use form MOH-F12. The claim must reach the accounts office by the 5th day of the following month; late claims are paid in the next payroll cycle [2].
rubric: Names form MOH-F12 and the 5th-of-month deadline; cites night duty allowance.

question: A patient's relative is asking for a copy of the patient's file. Can I give it to them?

context.title: Release of patient records
context.text: Patient records are released only with the written consent of the patient or on a court order. All requests are handled by the Medical Records Officer; no other staff member may release a record.

context.title: Gifts and hospitality
context.text: Any gift offered in connection with official duties must be declared in writing to the Head of Department within 7 days, whether or not it is accepted.

reference: No. Patient records are released only with the patient's written consent or on a court order, and only the Medical Records Officer may release them. Refer the relative to the Medical Records Officer [1].
rubric: Says no: only with written consent or a court order, via the Medical Records Officer.

question: When can I request a transfer to another duty station, and which form do I use?

context.title: Probation
context.text: Every newly appointed employee serves a probation period of 12 months. The supervisor completes a performance appraisal at the end of the sixth month and again before confirmation in post.

context.text: An employee may request a transfer after completing 3 years of service at the current duty station. The request is made on form MOH-T3 and submitted to the Human Resources Officer.
